findings.description: When agy opt-in is enabled, Google models that `routes_to_agy` under `cli-only` are no longer treated as CLI-routed for availability. The new gate only skips them when opt-in is off, but the later usability check still uses `cli_for`, which returns `agy` only for `gemini-headless`, not for routed Google model IDs like `gemini-2.5-pro`. That means a Google API credential can make a cli-only agy-routed voice look usable even when `agy` is not on PATH.
findings.failure_mode: The P3/adversarial review availability check can PASS with a Google credential but no agy CLI, then the actual planned headless route cannot run. This violates the shared routing rule introduced by the diff and can leave a configured review stage with no executable voice despite the preflight reporting one.
findings.suggested_fix: After computing `routes_to_agy "$m" "$p3_mode"`, use that routed result to force `cli=agy` for availability when opt-in is on, or add a shared helper that returns the effective transport/CLI for a model under the selected headless mode and use it for both gating and usability.

findings.description: The hunk introduces p3_mode (agy_headless_mode) and the shared routes_to_agy predicate, but consults them only to decide the gated-off case `(( ! p3_agy_on )) && routes_to_agy`. Once the opt-in is on, the usable-voice decision falls through to the pre-existing mode-blind pair: `cli=$(cli_for "$m")` (non-empty only for literal *-headless names) and otherwise `cred_present "$prov"`. Under `hounfour.headless.mode: cli-only` a Google voice such as `gemini-2.5-pro` or `google:gemini-3.1-pro` (rows the new conformance table marks routes_to_agy=True) therefore gets cli="" and is judged usable by a GOOGLE/GEMINI key, although the shared rule — the one this diff exists to adopt — says that voice dispatches through the `agy` binary and never touches the key. The same mismatch exists for the `gemini-headless:any` form: routes_to_agy returns True but the rewritten cli_for strips only a leading provider prefix and returns "" for a trailing `:suffix`, so with the opt-in on it is checked as a credential voice. (Context: the diff header labels this file adversarial-review.sh, but the hunk is the run-preflight P3 block; the P3 result also feeds STAGE_ONLY/P4 via `provs`.)
findings.failure_mode: cli-only + opt-in true + Gemini key set + no `agy` on PATH: P3 reports `code_review usable: gemini-2.5-pro` and PASSes; the review/Flatline run then starts and the voice fails at dispatch (PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE), i.e. a planned voice that cannot exist — the G-1 outcome the sprint is meant to make impossible. Inverse: cli-only + opt-in true + `agy` installed + no key → P3 marks the voice `missing` and FAILs a stage that would actually run.
findings.suggested_fix: After the gate, derive the resource from the same predicate instead of cli_for alone: e.g. `if routes_to_agy "$m" "$p3_mode"; then cli=agy; fi` (or make cli_for take the mode and delegate to agy-gate-lib), so the `command -v agy` branch is taken for every agy-routed voice and usable_names shows `(cli agy)`. Also normalise a trailing `:suffix` in cli_for (or reuse the lib's model-id normaliser) so `gemini-headless:any` maps to agy. Add a run-preflight.bats case: cli-only, opt-in true, key present, agy absent → FAIL/missing `(cli agy)`.

findings.anchor: tests/unit/agy-gate-conformance.bats:AGC-7 (case "$w" in bool) branch) and AGC-1 (`! agy_opted_in "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/missing.yaml"`)
findings.description: Two of the new conformance assertions are vacuous under bats/`set -e` semantics. In AGC-7 the boolean branch is `bool) [ "$output" = on ] && [ "$py" = on ] ;;` — a bare `&&` list. If the bash lib returns `off` for a boolean true, the first test fails, the list short-circuits, and because the failing command precedes `&&` neither `set -e` nor the ERR trap fires; the loop simply continues. Only the Python half (the final command of the list) can fail the test. In AGC-1, `! agy_opted_in "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/missing.yaml"` is a mid-test negation; bash exempts `!`-prefixed pipelines from `set -e`, so a lib that returned 0 on a missing file would pass unnoticed. Elsewhere the file correctly uses the `! cmd || { ...; return 1; }` idiom, so these two are inconsistencies rather than a pattern.
findings.failure_mode: A regression in agy_opted_in (boolean true → off in bash, or success on a missing config) is not caught by the suite that the SDD D-1.5/G12 rulings cite as the parity evidence; the report's 'every reader says so' claim rests partly on checks that cannot fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same guarded idiom as the rest of the file: `bool) [ "$output" = on ] && [ "$py" = on ] || { echo "bool: bash=$output py=$py"; return 1; } ;;` and `run ! agy_opted_in "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/missing.yaml"` (bats ≥1.5, already required) or `! agy_opted_in ... || { echo ...; return 1; }`.

findings.anchor: tests/unit/agy-gate-conformance.bats:AGC-9 (and the loa-status --json `! grep -q 'WARN'` check in AGC-8)
findings.description: AGC-9's environment isolation is inconsistent with its guard. The commands run with `PATH="/usr/bin:/bin:$(dirname "$(command -v yq)")"`, but the 'nothing available → silent' guard only checks `PATH="/usr/bin:/bin" command -v agy`. On any host where `agy` is installed next to yq (~/.local/bin, /usr/local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin — the usual case for both tools) the guard passes, the lib sees `agy` on PATH, and `[ -z "$stderr" ]` fails. The second assertion ('a Google/Gemini key is set') is not guarded at all and depends on `agy` being absent from the yq directory; if it is present the WARN reason may read 'agy on PATH' instead. If yq is the Python flavour (the P3 code still branches on YQ_FLAVOUR), its `jq` dependency must also be reachable from the restricted PATH. Separately, AGC-8 asserts `! grep -q 'WARN'` over the entire stderr of `loa-status.sh --json` run against the real repo with empty run/env dirs — any unrelated WARN emitted by loa-status (missing beads, missing CLI, etc.) fails the agy test.
findings.failure_mode: The suite is green on the implementer's host (where `agy` is absent, per the report) but fails or flakes on a host with `agy` installed or with loa-status emitting an unrelated WARN, eroding trust in the conformance suite that is cited as the D-1.5/D-1.7 evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute one restricted PATH variable (`rp="/usr/bin:/bin:$(dirname "$(command -v yq)")"`), use it for both the guard (`PATH="$rp" command -v agy`) and the runs, and apply the same guard (or `skip`) to the 'key is set' assertion. In AGC-8 grep for the specific agy WARN texts (`not a YAML boolean`, `agy route is available here`) rather than any `WARN`.

findings.trigger_anchor: tests/unit/agy-gate-conformance.bats:AGC-1 / AGC-7 (the `for v in absent false '"true"' 1 yes` loop vs the `_three` absent|bool|string set)
findings.cross_file_justification: The new conformance suite is the sole evidence that the bash lib and the Python twin agree on the opt-in value. AGC-1 pins bash as *off* for `yes` and `1`, but AGC-7 (the only test that feeds the Python reader) covers just absent / true / "true". yq (go, yaml.v3) resolves `agy_opt_in: yes` to !!str, whereas PyYAML's safe_load (YAML 1.1 schema) resolves yes/no/on/off to a boolean. If loader.py parses with PyYAML and tests `is True`, `agy_opt_in: yes` is ON for cheval and OFF for every bash planner.
findings.description: The parity table has a hole exactly where yq-go and PyYAML are known to disagree. The sprint's stated invariant (SDD D-1.5: ONE predicate; the AC: 'with the opt-in absent or false, cheval refuses … the dissent/Flatline/preflight record not planned') is only pinned on the bash side for YAML 1.1 booleans. An operator who writes `agy_opt_in: yes` (a very common YAML habit) would see `/loa` and run-preflight say 'opt-in (disabled)' while `cheval invoke --model gemini-headless` happily spawns `agy`; or the reverse, a dissent planner filtering a hop that cheval would have dispatched.
findings.failure_mode: Split-brain planning: bash planners mark the voice not planned (no companion runs, P3 FAILs the stage) while cheval, invoked directly or via a chain, treats the route as opted in and spawns `agy` — the unplanned spawn G-1 forbids. Unverified without loader.py in the diff, hence ADVISORY.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend AGC-7's `_three` set (or AGC-2's row list) with `yes`, `on`, `1` and `True` fed to both agy_opted_in and agy_opt_in_enabled, and make the Python predicate normalise the raw scalar like yq does (accept only a value the YAML 1.2 core schema tags as !!bool true, e.g. check the node tag with the loader's resolver or compare the raw token against true/True/TRUE) so both sides agree on every row.
